answer.label: Not sourced to Pope John Paul II — an unverified attribution
answer.authorDates: 1920–2005 · Pope, 1978–2005 · born Karol Wojtyła in Wadowice, Poland
answer.sourceLine: This one-line aphorism is credited to Pope John Paul II on dozens of quotation sites, but none give a source, and it appears nowhere in the Vatican’s archive of his encyclicals, homilies, and addresses, nor anywhere on Wikiquote. No speech, letter, or book has ever been tied to it, so the attribution is unsupported — treat it as apocryphal until a documented source surfaces.

author.name: Pope John Paul II
author.heading: About Pope John Paul II
author.bio: Karol Józef Wojtyła was Pope John Paul II from 1978 until his death in 2005, the first non-Italian pope in over four centuries and one of the most widely quoted religious figures of the modern era. His actual output — 14 encyclicals, thousands of addresses and homilies, and books such as Crossing the Threshold of Hope — is fully documented in the Vatican archive. That documented record is precisely why an unsourced one-liner like this one stands out as unverified.

cite.sourceCitation: No primary source located. Popularly circulated via quotation aggregators (BrainyQuote, Goodreads, AZQuotes, Quotefancy); absent from the Vatican archive of John Paul II’s writings and addresses and from Wikiquote. Earliest documented usage: unestablished.

misattribution.heading: A famous name, an empty citation
misattribution.intro: Pope John Paul II is one of the internet’s most reliable magnets for tidy, uplifting lines that no one can source — and this is one of them. Every site that credits him repeats the attribution; none produce the document.

items.why: Quote sites from BrainyQuote to Goodreads attach his name with no speech, date, or text, and the line is absent from the Vatican’s record of his words.
The line does not appear on his Wikiquote page at all — not in the sourced section, and not flagged as misattributed. It simply isn’t part of his documented sayings.

misattribution.truthLine: No document, no date, no speech: the honest verdict is that this is an unsourced attribution, consistent with his general outlook but not demonstrably his words.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: The sentiment — that the future is built by what you do now, not by intentions deferred to ‘tomorrow’ — is an ancient commonplace, close in spirit to countless proverbs about seizing the day. That familiarity is part of why a name like John Paul II’s sticks to it so easily: the line sounds like something he could have said.

But sounding right is not evidence. Pope John Paul II left an unusually complete paper trail, and this exact wording is nowhere in it. Until a genuine source appears, the responsible label is ‘unverified,’ not ‘said by Pope John Paul II.’
context.pull: Sounding like something he could have said is not evidence that he did.
